cells.tense: Right now the pieces are in your hands and the order is yours to set.
cells.ask: Take one thing you're tending and put its next three steps on paper today, then do the first.
cells.core:
You're holding several threads about something you're growing, and you can see how they fit. Most people carry threads like these and leave them in a heap. You put them in order.

It shows in how you talk about what you're tending. You don't list worries, you sequence them: this first, that next, this one waits. That's quiet, steady work, and whatever you're bringing along gets the benefit of it. The same clear eye is available for you when the question is what you owe or what you're owed — the answer tends to arrive fast and without much arithmetic. Run with it rather than checking it again. The plan has been reviewed enough. What it wants now is a first step, taken today.
cells.sheetLine: You can see how the pieces fit. Act like it.
cells.verb: Gathering scattered thoughts into one shape
cells.place: Where something young is being tended

cells.tense: You are already living in a version of this that hasn't happened yet.
cells.ask: Pick the one next step that's actually available today and do only that, leaving the rest unscheduled.
cells.core:
You're trying to get the whole picture right before anything moves. Somewhere ahead is the version where every part is accounted for and nothing can go wrong, and you're bracing for it — adding plans, checking them, adding more. The thing you're tending doesn't need the finished picture. It needs a next step.

There's care in all that preparation, real care, and it's starting to crowd out the thing itself. Growing doesn't wait for certainty. When you push the plan ahead of the pace of what's actually happening, you end up managing instead of tending. What sits under the urgency is feeling — yours about this — and that's the thing worth steering by, more than the fear of missing something. One true step beats five prepared ones.

cells.tense: The door you're standing at has already closed behind you.
cells.ask: Tell one person one thing you're actually growing right now, in plain words, and let their response land before you answer it.
cells.core:
There's something you've been caring for and you've stopped pulling your thoughts together about it. The threads are still there. You just haven't picked them up. You describe it as fine, or as handled, and that description has gotten further from the truth over time.

The care didn't leave. What stopped is the gathering. When you don't bring the thoughts into one place, everything about the thing feels like too much at once, so you look away from all of it, and looking away has started to feel like the safe choice. Plenty of feeling is still moving through — it just has nowhere to sit without a shape. Let one person hear it plainly. Not to fix it. Just to have it said where someone can see it.
cells.sheetLine: The care is still there. The gathering stopped.

cells.tense: You are already tending this well and calling it nothing in particular.
cells.ask: Name one thing you've been growing, out loud, as yours, and say what you want for it.
cells.core:
You're doing the gathering already — noticing what's off, checking what's fair, holding the threads about something you're growing. It runs in the background, and you talk about it like it's just how things went. The work is happening. You haven't signed it.

That matters more than it sounds. When the care goes unnamed, it can't be shared, and the thing you're growing ends up with nobody standing behind it — including you. Fairness is tangled up in this too. You've been giving attention without counting it, then wondering why it feels like no one's keeping score. Somebody is keeping score. You are. Say what you're growing and what you want for it, where it can be heard. Not a report. Just yours, said out loud.
